task.title: Compose Quality Gates and Publish the Suite Verdict

metrics.coverageNote: This task composes existing measured gates and CI evidence; coverage was not re-measured, so null is reported rather than a fabricated percentage.

tdd.red: scripts/verification/publish-verdict.test.ts was written before production code and failed because ./publish-verdict did not exist. After the compositor was implemented, publication semantics were green while the CI-retention scenario remained RED because suite-verdict was absent from ci.yml.
tdd.green: The runner-output authority boundary, six-gate composition, exclusive evidence sink, blocking CI job, and always-uploaded 30-day artifact made all focused scenarios pass.
tdd.refactor: Gate execution, composition, and publication are separate boundaries. Captured signals and verdicts are frozen, advisory outcomes have their own closed value, evidence logs are digest-addressed, and no verdict-input or from-JSON path exists.

acceptance.criterion: One verdict per run names every gate, its outcome and evidence reference, with advisory outcomes never counted as pass
acceptance.evidence: composeQualityGates requires typecheck, traceability, quarantine, conformance, coverage, and flake exactly once; the production run also includes the suite signal. Every gate records explicit blocking policy, pass/fail/advisory outcome, command, exit code, log reference and SHA-256. Advisory entries are excluded from both pass count and pass-rate denominator.

acceptance.criterion: The verdict is parsed from runner and gate output; a hand-authored or self-reported verdict is rejected
acceptance.evidence: Only executeGate can mint an admitted signal from command exit/stdout/stderr; composeQualityGates rejects an identically shaped authored object. The CLI exposes no verdict JSON input and always executes the declared commands itself. Raw stdout/stderr and exit code are persisted beside the verdict.

acceptance.criterion: Published verdicts are append-only and retained as CI artifacts
acceptance.evidence: publishSuiteVerdict creates .verification/run/<runId>.json and its evidence directory exclusively and refuses an existing run id without changing prior bytes. CI uploads .verification/run/ under a run-id/run-attempt artifact name with if: always() and retention-days: 30.

verification.focusedAndRelated: PASS - 31 tests, 0 failures, 123 expect() calls across publisher, CI topology, flake ledger and documentation reconciliation
verification.workflowSyntax: PASS - PyYAML safe_load, eight jobs including suite-verdict
verification.fullPublisherCLI: NOT RUN LOCALLY - by design it executes the full suite, pinned typecheck, traceability, quarantine, conformance, coverage and flake gates serially. The authority/publishing boundary is covered with injected runner output; CI owns the real end-to-end execution. No end-to-end success is claimed from this bounded Phase-B run.

decisions: The Suite Run itself is included as a seventh blocking signal in production in addition to the six gates the task explicitly requires. A red suite therefore cannot coexist with a green Suite Verdict.
The suite-verdict job reruns checks instead of composing GitHub job status labels. Job labels are orchestration metadata, not runner/gate output, and using them would violate ADR-0021.
Advisory is an outcome, not a successful exit relabelled as pass. It never increments passed and never enters the pass-rate denominator.
The verdict sink is ephemeral and git-ignored; CI artifact retention, not repository commits, preserves each per-run record for 30 days.
Project-memory updated the digest and reconciled docs/README.md with the PRD nodes already present in docs/.graph.json. No new documentation node was created.

scopeNotes.phaseC: No adversarial QA, architectural review, optimization loop, or Phase C validation was performed.
scopeNotes.ephemeralOutput: .verification/run is intentionally ignored; tests publish only into isolated temporary roots and leave no workspace verdict artifact.
scopeNotes.preservedPriorWork: All prior dirty workflow, probe, ledger, documentation, and report changes were preserved.
